chunks: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about a man whose wife became pure from her menstruation, and he said, 'So-and-so is divorced,' while a group of people heard his words, and he did not say to them, 'Bear witness.' Would the divorce take effect upon her? He said, 'Yes, this is a testimony.'

key_terms.طَهُرَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ: The wife becoming pure from menstruation

ai.seo_question: Does a casual divorce declaration require an explicit command to witness for it to be valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that a casual declaration of divorce ('So-and-so is divorced') made in the presence of listeners, even without explicitly commanding them to bear witness, is considered sufficient for the divorce to take effect. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the presence of witnesses who hear the declaration serves as implicit testimony, distinguishing it from the stricter requirements of some Sunni schools that demand an explicit 'I testify' formula. This hadith underscores the importance of verbal intent and auditory confirmation in marital dissolution within the Ahl al-Bayt tradition.
